judged_text: The SalesforceCalendarService constructor now refreshes its OAuth token unconditionally on every service instantiation — issuing a token refresh request to login.salesforce.com and a prisma.credential.update with no expiry check (previously jsforce refreshed on demand) — burning Salesforce token-endpoint calls and API limits, adding a DB write per operation (services are constructed per credential per operation), and making every Salesforce calendar operation fail if the token endpoint hiccups or rate-limits, even when credential-sharing is disabled.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs a refresh-token grant to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then immediately `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning the `jsforce.Connection` (see the newly added `fetch(...)` + `await prisma.credential.update(...)` block right after `const credentialKey = ...`). There is no expiry/validity check and no guard around credential-sharing flags; so every instantiation will incur a network call + DB write and will fail early if the token endpoint errors/rate-limits, even if an existing access token would have been sufficient. This is a concrete, diff-grounded reliability/performance/architecture concern, but not a strictly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.
